sections.content: You know *seguir* + gerund from A2 Unit 28: *Sigo trabajando aquí* means "I am still working here". The action has not stopped, and it is the opposite of *dejar de* + infinitive (you know *dejar de* from B1 Unit 12). B2 adds two things. First, *seguir sin* + infinitive says that something still has not happened: *Sigo sin saber la respuesta* is "I still don't know the answer". Second, *seguir* in the past often shows that something went on in spite of a difficulty: *Aunque llovía, seguimos caminando*.
sections.title: You know it, with two additions
Seguir in different shapes
rows: Sigo viviendo en el mismo barrio.
I still live in the same neighbourhood.
Mi tío sigue sin hablar con su vecino.
My uncle still isn't speaking to his neighbour.
Although it was raining, we kept on walking.
You were still sleeping when I called.

sections.content: After *sin* the verb is always an infinitive: *Sigo sin saber*, never *Sigo sin sabiendo*. *Continuar* + gerund means the same as *seguir* + gerund and sounds a little more formal: *Los vecinos continuaron hablando*. Remember too that *seguir* can take an adjective or a place instead of a gerund: *Sigue enfermo*, *Sigue aquí*.
